solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Again treats broken bone with supports around centre of humerus

indicators.note: the word for supports goes around the letter taken from the bone's name

parts.note: rests are props or supports, as for a billiard cue

indicators.note: the centre of a seven-letter word is its fourth letter, the middle of humerus

explanation.surface: An orthopaedic surgeon redoes a fracture, propping it up around the upper arm bone.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor who sets a broken bone a second time does it again, the medical sense of setting a fracture.

clue.text: Cheer wildly over coming last — one wants repeat

indicators.note: the over's letter comes at the end, after the rearranged cheer
cheering done wildly is disordered, so the five letters of the cheer are rearranged

parts.note: O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A crowd cheers wildly at the end of the cricket over and someone shouts for an encore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' rearranges CHEER to REECH; O comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: To sound again, as a voice off a cliff wall, is to repeat a noise once more.

clue.text: Peer intently, we're told, to see flight's location

indicators.note: what we are told is heard spoken, so the phrase for peering is said out loud

parts.note: to peer intently is to stare well, looking hard

explanation.surface: Look hard, someone advises, if you want to spot where the aircraft has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' looks like an aeroplane trip but is a flight of steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of stairs runs up the vertical shaft built to house it inside a building.

clue.text: It's dry round here with nothing else

indicators.note: the two letters for teetotal go round the word here

parts.note: TT, teetotal, describes someone who keeps dry
O is the round shape of zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A wry remark that this place is dry and has nothing more on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: The old adverb means besides or in addition to that, so it can stand for else in a list.

clue.text: Wine frothing upset hosting staff

indicators.note: the rearranged letters host, or hold inside them, the word for staff
frothing is bubbling and churning, so the letters of upset are churned into a new order

parts.note: to man a post is to staff it

explanation.surface: A sparkling wine foaming over and spilling onto the waiters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frothing' rearranges the letters of 'upset' to SPUTE; 'hosting' puts the staff word inside. 'upset' looks like the anagram signal but is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian sparkling white wine, the best known being from Asti in Piedmont.

clue.text: Foreboding I ignored for theatrical performance?

indicators.note: the letter I is ignored, left out of the word for foreboding

parts.note: a presentiment is a feeling that something will happen, a foreboding

explanation.surface: A dread of something bad, brushed aside before a stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: A presentment is a presentation or depiction, here pictured as something presented on stage, hence the question mark.

clue.text: More than one conductor's no good in jazzy ragtimes

indicators.note: jazzy suggests a lively improvised reworking, so the remaining letters are shuffled
no good means without the letter for good, so it is struck from ragtimes

explanation.surface: Several bandleaders turn out to be poor at playing jazzed-up ragtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' drops G from RAGTIMES, leaving RATIMES, which 'jazzy' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian plural of the word for a master musician, used of orchestral conductors.

clue.text: Lack of territory limited 'Observer'

parts.note: no, as in no money, signals a lack

indicators.note: the word territory is limited, cut short to its first three letters

explanation.surface: A newspaper headline complaining that a land has too little ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limited' trims TERRITORY to TER; 'Observer' looks like the Sunday paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who notes things down or takes notice of them is an observer.

clue.text: After a good 23, see this?

parts.note: after a good private chat (the answer to 23) two people come to agree, and you see this phrase in the idiom of agreeing

explanation.surface: A cross-reference teaser: what you see after a satisfying private chat.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 is TETE-A-TETE; after a good one you 'see' this, completing the idiom for agreeing.
explanation.definitionFit: To see this way with someone is the idiom for being in full agreement.

clue.text: The Spanish holding reputation for paint

indicators.note: the Spanish article holds the word for reputation inside it

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
a good name is a good reputation

explanation.surface: A Spanish firm famous for its paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamel is a glossy hard-drying paint, as used on metal and radiators.

clue.text: Light again on Bench

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading
a settle is a long wooden bench with a high back

explanation.surface: A judge brought back to the bench, or a lamp switched on again.
explanation.definitionFit: To light is to alight or come to rest, as a bird does, so to light again is to come down once more.

clue.text: Filly's standing by weed? That's lucky

indicators.note: the word for weeding stands by, next to, the horse word

parts.note: a filly is a horse, and filly's stands for horse is
to hoe is to weed with a garden tool

explanation.surface: A young mare grazing beside a weed, and someone thinks that is a good omen.
explanation.definitionFit: A horseshoe hung over a door is a traditional charm for good fortune.

clue.text: Checking bleeding with article in mobile home? Not mobile

indicators.note: the article sits in the rearranged home
mobile means moving about, so the letters of home move into a new order

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
something static is fixed, not mobile

explanation.surface: A first-aider stopping bleeding with an item found in a caravan that cannot move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mobile' rearranges to HEMO, and 'in' puts the article inside it, giving HAEMO, the British spelling for blood.
explanation.definitionFit: A haemostatic drug or dressing stops blood flowing from a wound.

clue.text: Royal Society cutting also in trunk

indicators.note: the society's initials cut into the word for also

parts.note: too means also
RS is the abbreviation for the Royal Society, Britain's science academy

explanation.surface: Scientists slicing up a tree trunk as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trunk' looks like a tree's but is the human body without limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the body's trunk, the part left without head and limbs.

clue.text: Travelling in city cortège — one with it is 17

indicators.note: the letters travel about, moving into a new order

explanation.surface: A funeral procession moving through town, with a pompous mourner aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is FULL OF ONESELF: anyone who has this trait is full of themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-centredness is the trait of those who are full of themselves, thinking only of their own importance.

clue.text: In European court, engaged in split, with different ending?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the European court letters are engaged, fitted, in the word for split

parts.note: to split is slang for to leave, to have fled

explanation.surface: A divided European court case that ended differently than expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'split' means ran off, FLED, not divided.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar a word inflected for case or tense has its ending changed, as walk becomes walked.

clue.text: Top fifes played away from the beaten track

indicators.note: played suggests the letters are performed in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The best fife players marching off the usual parade route.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiing off the groomed runs is skiing away from the trodden course, figuratively anything unconventional.

clue.text: Self-important as an auto-cannibal may be?

definitions.meaning: conceited, vain and pleased with oneself
someone who eats themselves would literally be stuffed with their own flesh

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means conceited, and literally describes someone whose belly holds their own body.

clue.text: Across the Channel, perhaps, manage to be heard

indicators.note: the word for manage is to be heard, spoken out loud

parts.note: to oversee a project is to manage it

explanation.surface: Someone running a business on the other side of the Channel, making a noise about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Overseas means abroad, and for Britain the nearest abroad is across the English Channel, hence perhaps.

clue.text: Story for American engineers making piece of furniture

parts.note: étage is French for a floor; story is the American spelling of storey
RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army's engineering corps

explanation.surface: A tale written for American engineers about making a cabinet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Story' looks like a tale; with 'for American' it is the US spelling of storey, a floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A whatnot, a set of open display shelves standing one above another.

clue.text: Fish cocktail

definitions.meaning: the rudd, a freshwater fish with ...
a drink of beer and tomato juice, sometimes with a raw egg

explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a freshwater fish and to a beer-and-tomato-juice hangover drink.

clue.text: Smoother grade of life?

definitions.meaning: a carpenter's tool for smoothing wood
a level of existence, as in a higher state of being

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a woodworking tool for levelling and also a level of existence or development.

clue.text: Old saying of publicity era

parts.note: an ad, short for advertisement, is publicity
an age is an era

explanation.surface: A slogan from the golden age of advertising.
explanation.definitionFit: A proverb or maxim handed down over a long time.

clue.text: Private chat in French kissing position?

definitions.meaning: an intimate conversation between two people
in French the phrase is literally head to head, the way two people stand to kiss

explanation.definitionFit: The French loan phrase means a one-to-one talk, and literally head-to-head, as a kissing couple are.

clue.text: Scattered state school initially quiet with five leaving Oxbridge, say

indicators.note: initially points at the first letter of school

parts.note: p is the musical marking piano, quiet

indicators.note: the numeral is leaving, taken out of the word for university

parts.note: varsity is an old word for university, Oxford or Cambridge for instance
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A state school goes quiet after five pupils depart for Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like part of 'state school' but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thinly spread or scattered is the condition of sparseness.

clue.text: One carrying out sting is clear of all charges by the French

parts.note: nett, the British spelling of net, means after all deductions
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A con artist who pulls off a sting walks free, cleared by the French court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sting' suggests a police operation; it is the plant's burning hairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A stinging plant whose hairs inject an irritant into skin is a thing that delivers a sting.

clue.text: Refinement, for example, found in Eastern weapon

indicators.note: the abbreviation is found inside the word for weapon

parts.note: a lance is a long cavalry spear
eg is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Polished style, as seen in a finely crafted oriental weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegance is grace and polish of manner or style, a synonym of refinement.

clue.text: Be regularly sandalled as mace-bearer

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of sandalled, the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: Be sure to wear sandals when carrying the ceremonial mace.
explanation.definitionFit: A beadle is a parish or university officer who carries a mace in ceremonial processions.
